origin.rerun: Re-read .github/workflows/training-rerun-5m.yml's `on: push:` block; confirm whether a `branches:` allowlist (or a path restriction limited to a training-plan-scoped branch pattern) has been added, and whether `git push origin HEAD:${{ github.ref_name }}` has been guarded against pushing to a branch outside that allowlist.

what: MEDIUM (incidental, not CA-B02 scope): .github/workflows/training-rerun-5m.yml's `push` trigger has no `branches:` filter and matches ANY branch touching experiments/2026-05-07-vwap-accuracy/{run_5m.py,fetch_data.py} or the workflow file itself; it then commits its results 'back to the same branch as the triggering push' (git push origin HEAD:${{ github.ref_name }}). Observed live: merging origin/main into PR #13200's branch (claude/ca-b02-audit) picked up an unrelated PR's edit to this workflow file, which triggered training-rerun-5m.yml to run AND commit a 'TRAINING-RESULTS: 2026-05-07-vwap-accuracy 5m re-run' result commit directly onto claude/ca-b02-audit -- a docs-only code-audit PR with nothing to do with the vwap experiment. Had to be reverted (commit c07ba5f) to keep the audit PR's diff clean. Any PR that merges main and picks up a change to that workflow file (or the two experiment files) is exposed to the same contamination, regardless of what the PR is actually about.
